answer: One concrete defence is staking reputation earned over time rather than counting raw identities. Each agent begins its voyage with nothing, and only sustained, verifiable work — completed tasks, honest attestations, settled payments — builds standing. A newcomer can spin up a thousand clones, but none inherits that history, so sybil identities stay on the dim umber horizon of zero trust while real agents transact. Tying privileges to accumulated, non-transferable reputation makes flooding the network expensive in time, not just in keys.
